findings.text: Central futex dispatcher validates clock and robust flag combinations before branching on the masked command to wait, wake, requeue, compare-requeue, wake-op, inheritance lock and unlock helpers and requeue-PI paths, normalizing legacy wait and wake forms to bitset variants and forcing realtime clock for classic lock-PI; unknown commands fail.

Legacy futex entry preprocesses an optional user timeout only for commands that accept one, applying failure injection and user copy checks, converting the timespec through a helper that distinguishes relative classic wait from absolute others with namespace adjustment, then forwards the deadline and remaining arguments to the central dispatcher.

Wait-on-many entry rejects nonzero flags and out-of-range counts, optionally arms an absolute timer for realtime or monotonic clocks, allocates a per-futex descriptor array, parses user descriptors with a shared validator, blocks in the multi-wait core, then releases the array and tears down the timer.

Wake-only modern entry validates the caller mask against the version-two allowed set, translates it to internal flag representation with strict checking, then invokes the common wake helper for the given address, count and mask.

Robust-list query entry resolves the target head for the given process identifier in non-create mode, propagates lookup failures, then copies the head size and pointer to user space, failing on copy errors.

Reader-writer semaphore wakeup serializes queue inspection under the waiter spinlock with interrupt state preserved, delegates head evaluation to a marking helper when a waiter exists, releases the lock, then drains a local wake queue outside the critical section and returns the semaphore.

Realtime read-base unlock uses only an atomic decrement in the fast path and takes the underlying mutex waiter lock with interrupts disabled only when the last reader departs, capturing the current owner for deferred wakeup while holding preemption disabled across unlock and queue drain; the generic read-unlock wrapper delegates to this path.

Wake-operation helper resolves two futex keys for read and write access, acquires both hash-bucket locks in a defined double-lock order, performs the user atomic operation while holding them, scans each bucket chain for matching waiters, then releases both locks before draining wakeups.

Multi-wait setup pins the private hash across the whole operation, resolves all keys before changing task state to avoid sleeping while queued, then locks one hash bucket at a time to validate the user value and enqueue, never holding a bucket lock while resolving the next key.

Reader-ownership and non-spinnable handling exists in active and empty build variants; active forms preserve flag bits while setting or clearing ownership with atomic operations, including a compare-exchange retry that only clears when the current task owns the semaphore, while alternate forms and the debug warning macro compile to no-ops and the realtime ownership test derives state from a negative reader count distinct from a bias value.

Reader wakeup grants are bounded per call, adjust the semaphore count by bias multiples, and clear waiter and handoff flags when the queue empties or when readers have been granted, while refusing new reader grants when the count indicates writer dominance and requesting handoff after a waiter timeout.

Futex flag validation restricts realtime-clock use and robust-unlock use to small command subsets, enforces shared versus private retry paths, applies strict checking on modern wake, and rejects zero bitsets, out-of-range shift amounts, unknown comparisons, and descriptors with reserved bits or invalid values.

Waiters form a circular doubly linked list anchored by a first-waiter pointer; a helper returns the successor in list order or null on wrap-around, requires the waiter lock to be held, and wakeup collection moves granted readers to a temporary list while advancing the anchor.

Multi-wait descriptors pair per-futex wait parameters of flags, expected value and address with an initialized queue node carrying key, bitset and wake callback, while single wait on interruptible exit records address, value, absolute time, bitset and timeout-present flags into the task restart block for later resume.

Mark-wake distinguishes a writer-headed queue that only wakes the head writer on any-wake requests from a reader-headed queue that performs an early single-reader grant with writer-steal detection, then enters collect-then-wake phases where eligible readers are counted and accounted before any task pointer is cleared and queued for wakeup.

Single futex wait progresses through timer arming, setup that holds the bucket lock on success, sleeping until wakeup, timeout or signal, and unqueue-based outcome classification where dequeued means success, expired timer means timeout, pending signal means restartable interruption, and otherwise the cycle repeats as a spurious wakeup.

Multi-wait loops over setup returning success, value-mismatch, fault or already-woken index, followed by a sleep that is skipped if any queue already dequeued or the timer fired, then unqueue scanning that returns the highest dequeued index on success and otherwise maps timer expiry and signals to timeout and restart statuses with retry on spurious events.

Several races are closed by ordering: reader task references are acquired before clearing the waiter pointer with release semantics and safe queueing; count increments precede wakeups via two passes; writer steal during first grant aborts with rollback; user faults during locked reads trigger unlock, unwind of already queued entries, fault handling without locks, and full retry.

Timeout acceptance is an ABI property limited to classic wait, PI lock variants, bitset wait and PI requeue wait; modern wait-on-many accepts only realtime and monotonic clock identifiers, and legacy classic wait interprets its timeout as relative while other absolute timeouts undergo monotonic namespace conversion except for realtime and classic PI lock.

Wake-operation encoding packs operation, comparison and two signed eleven-bit immediates into fixed bit fields with an optional shift-to-mask transformation of the first immediate clamped to word width, and comparison codes cover equality, inequality and four ordered relations with any other code rejected.

Wake-operation rejects buckets containing priority-inheritance or realtime waiter state, treats non-fault atomic errors as terminal while fault-related errors trigger user fault-in, voluntary rescheduling and key re-resolution with a private-only fast retry versus full retry for shared futexes.
